## Is a smaller copy worth keeping? (`harness/compression_test.py keep`)

9 masters × factors 2 and 3. Damage = Butteraugli against the true small image (the master shrunk with Pillow Lanczos), at the small copy's size: the large file shrunk the same way, the small copy as it is. Max-norm ≥ 1 counts as visible (libjxl's "just noticeable"). "+jpegQS" = restored with jpegQS -q 6.

## Can a re-saved JPEG be recognised? (`harness/jpeg_history.py --test`)

9 masters × 10 histories. "Flagged" = the ghost or the shifted-grid check finds an earlier save. On a one-time save a flag is a false alarm unless the master itself came from a JPEG: the q95 flags are the lion and Hokusai masters, crops of q≈90 JPEGs, found at their crop offsets (x+2, and x+5 y+1). The grid check needs textured blocks the decoder did not clip, which pure black-and-white art (the line art, the manga page) lacks.
